decisions.reason: Product A builds on an established offer and has shown no below-aspiration shortfall, so problemistic search is not triggered and slack allows continued evaluation.
Product B aligns with the firm's strategic carrier wafer direction and shows no evidence of aspiration shortfalls, so management keeps it for market learning.
Product C is a stated flagship and builds on established capabilities, so despite some uncertainty management keeps it and uses slack to support its strategic direction.
Product D is close to the established offer and presented as a flagship brand, so its results likely meet aspirations and the firm keeps the product line.
Product E is distant from the firm's established offer and its likely below-aspiration results trigger problemistic search, so management drops it to reallocate resources.
